title: Sap Is Running, So Are We
skyStory: The crescent moon swells to twenty-eight percent in Taurus, the sign of comfort and good things slowly made. Down in the hardwoods, the maple sap has started to run, drip by drip into metal pails. Venus counts every drop with deep satisfaction. The moon leans in to smell the steam rising off the sugar shacks and sighs. Sweetness takes time, it says. Lots of time.

reading: It takes about forty buckets of sap to make one bucket of syrup, and that is the whole lesson for today. Your best work is not quick. It is boiled down, slowly, until only the good part remains. Stop rushing the pot.

The cabin wants you to do one thing the slow way today: hand-write a note, cook something that simmers, fix a thing properly instead of taping it. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] reversed has been teaching you that slowness is not a punishment. It is the recipe. By late afternoon you will taste the difference, and the Tiger will lie by the stove looking extremely pleased with itself.
joel.mission: Do one task today deliberately slowly, the old-fashioned way, from start to finish without checking your phone even once.
joel.omen: Steam rising from a pot, puddle or roof in sunshine. It means something you have been patient with is nearly ready.

reading: Taurus energy suits you: steady, earthy, and in no particular hurry. Today you will feel like making something cozy happen, a slow lunch, a warm room, an afternoon with nowhere to be. Follow the feeling. The Wood Rat has earned a nest day.

Somewhere in the afternoon a smell will hit you, woodsmoke, maple, or warm bread, and bring back a memory so vivid it feels like time travel. Let it. Tell somebody the story, with full hand choreography. Your storytelling magic works best when it starts from a sense like smell. People will lean in. Even the moon leans in, all twenty-eight percent of it.
nancy.mission: Tell one person a story today that begins with the phrase this smell reminds me of, and use both hands.
nancy.omen: The scent of woodsmoke drifting from nowhere in particular. It means a happy memory is about to become useful again.

together.text: Sugar season is here. Each of you describe to the other, in loving detail, the best warm thing you have ever smelled cooking. Make it rich and slow, like the sap. The listener must respond only with a long, satisfied mmm.

game.intro: Sap is running and so is the crew. Spell it in little pictures, no letters, sticky fingers allowed.
game.prompt: A breakfast you'd make for a cabin full of sleepy friends.
